SHE HELPED GENERAL AVIATION TAKE ITS PLACE IN HISTORY. ✈️

Dorothy S. Cochrane spent nearly five decades helping people discover the extraordinary stories behind everyday flying. Now Women in Aviation International has selected her for its 2027 Pioneer Hall of Fame.

Cochrane joined the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum in 1977 as one of its first female curators. Her work brought general aviation and women’s aviation history into the spotlight—including the Thomas W. Haas “We All Fly” gallery, which opened in 2022.

She also helped bring Patty Wagstaff’s Extra 260 into the national collection and recorded the experiences of 15 pioneering military women aviators through an oral history initiative.

After retiring in 2025, she’ll be honored in Savannah on February 26, 2027.

Aviation needs people who fly, build and maintain airplanes—and people who make sure their stories inspire the next generation. Here’s to one of them. 💛

Source: Women in Aviation International, October 29, 2026.
